turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you in?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've just been having uh, this pain in my um right, right elbow, and it's just been getting worse over the last few days. I started having it around three days ago. Um, and it's just been getting worse with any kind of gripping motion or, yeah, so it's, it's been getting worse.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, so you said it started three days ago. Um, has it been persistent since, or has it been like on and off?

turns.text: It's been pretty persistent, um, but it's mainly when I'm uh, doing some activities or lifting anything. Um, and yes, I've just been trying to rest it mostly.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, okay, that's good. And um, you said it's worse with activity and better with rest. Have you tried anything else for it?

turns.label: Patient

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, um, and if you were to describe the quality of this pain, would you say it's sharp, burning, throbbing, achy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's more um, like if I don't extend my wrist, it's kind of like achy, but then if I extend my wrist, I feel like a sharp pain at um, on the um, just on the outside of my elbow.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, alright. Um alright, and then um, in terms of severity, 1 to 10, 10 being the worst pain you've ever felt, how bad is the pain?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, so um, it sounds like you have something called tennis elbow or lateral epicondylitis. Um, and so basically for this, um, we suggest a few things. We'll start with like some conservative management, like activity modification. So at work, if you're doing repetitive movements, maybe not do them so much and take frequent breaks, you can try some like ibuprofen, we'll refer you to some um, physiotherapy to help build those muscles around that, that area.
